#The ggplot2 package helps us create graphs in R.

A `geom` tells R what type of graph to draw.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

We will use the `mtcars` dataset.( it is a build in dataset)


## geom_point() – Scatter plot

Shows the relationship between two variables.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()
```

## geom_line() – Line graph

Shows changes or trends, especially over time.

```{r}
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_line()
```

##geom_bar() – Bar chart

Counts how many items are in each group.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar()
```

## geom_col() – Column chart

Shows numbers that we already have.

```{r}
sales <- data.frame(
  product = c("Books", "Phones", "Computers"),
  amount = c(30, 45, 25)
)

ggplot(sales, aes(x = product, y = amount)) +
  geom_col()
```

#Here not that geom_bar()` is for counts; `geom_col()` uses given numbers.

#geom_histogram() – this is used for Histogram ,Shows how numerical values are distributed.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10)
```

## geom_boxplot() – Boxplot

Compares values between groups.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

## geom_density() – Density plot

#Shows the shape of a data distribution.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_density()
```

## geom_smooth() – Trend line

#Shows the general relationship or trend between two variables.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

##geom_violin() – Violin plot

Shows the distribution of values in different groups.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_violin()
```

## geom_area() – Area graph

Shows a trend with the area under the line filled.

```{r}
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_area()
```
